 Harekrushna Mahatab (Utkal Keshari) 1899-1987, Biography, Contributions
 Harekrushna Mahatab Birth Anniversary 2026 marks his 127th birth anniversary on 21 November. Read about the Odisha freedom fighter's biography, legacy and contributions.

 Harekrushna Mahatab was a prominent freedom fighter, political leader and literary figure from Odisha. Known as Utkal Keshari, he played an important role in India’s independence movement and the political integration of Odisha. His contributions as Chief Minister, administrator and social reformer shaped the state’s development. 
 Harekrushna Mahatab Birth Anniversary 2026 
 Harekrushna Mahatab Birth Anniversary 2026 will be observed on 21 November 2026 , marking his 127th birth anniversary . Remembered as Utkal Keshari, he made significant contributions to India’s freedom struggle, Odisha’s political integration, social reform and administrative development. 
 Harekrushna Mahatab Biography 
 Harekrushna Mahatab was born on 21 November 1899 in Agarpada village, present day Bhadrak district, Odisha. 
 Early Life: He was born to Krushna Charan Das and Tohapha Debi. He completed matriculation from Bhadrak High School and joined Ravenshaw College, Cuttack, for higher education. 
 Entry into Freedom Movement: In 1921, he left college to participate in the freedom struggle. He was arrested in 1922 on sedition charges and imprisoned several times for his nationalist activities. 
 Political Leadership: He served as Chairman of the Balasore District Board from 1924 to 1928 and became a member of the Bihar and Odisha Council. 
 Role in National Movement: He participated in the Salt Satyagraha in 1930 and the Quit India Movement in 1942, remaining imprisoned from 1942 to 1945. 
 Congress Association: Subhas Chandra Bose nominated him to the Congress Working Committee in 1938. He also served as President of the Utkal Pradesh Congress Committee. 
 Chief Minister and Other Positions: He served as Odisha’s Chief Minister from 1946 to 1950 and 1956 to 1960. He also held the Union Commerce and Industry portfolio and served as Governor of Bombay. 
 Later Political Career: He became an MP from Angul in 1962 and Congress Vice President in 1966. Later, he founded and led the Orissa Jana Congress and was imprisoned during the Emergency in 1976. 
 Death: Harekrushna Mahatab passed away on 2 January 1987.

 Harekrushna Mahatab Contributions 
 Harekrushna Mahatab made lasting contributions to Odisha through political integration, infrastructure development, social reform, the freedom movement and literature. 
 Integration of Princely States: He played a significant role in integrating former princely states with Odisha, strengthening the state’s territorial and administrative unity after independence. 
 Development of Bhubaneswar: During his tenure as Chief Minister, he facilitated the shifting of Odisha’s capital from Cuttack to Bhubaneswar, supporting the state’s administrative development. 
 Hirakud Dam Project: He contributed to the sanction and construction of the Hirakud Dam Project, an important multipurpose river valley project supporting irrigation and regional development. 
 Fight Against Untouchability: In 1934, he opened the gates of his ancestral temple to people from all communities, taking a significant step towards social equality and the removal of untouchability. 
 Contribution to Journalism: He founded the weekly Prajatantra in 1923, which later became a daily newspaper. He also edited Jhankar and the English weekly The Eastern Times. 
 Literary Contributions: He authored several literary works, including Gaon Majlis. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1983 for its third volume. 
 Promotion of Literature and Culture: He served as President of the Odisha Sahitya Akademi and Sangeet Natak Akademi, contributing to the promotion of literature, performing arts and cultural activities. 
 Legacy: Popularly known as the Lion of Odisha and Utkal Keshari . His contributions remain significant in Odisha’s political, social and literary history.

 Harekrushna Mahatab FAQs 
 Q1. Who was Harekrushna Mahatab? + 
 Ans . Harekrushna Mahatab was an Indian freedom fighter, political leader, writer and former Chief Minister of Odisha, popularly known as Utkal Keshari.
 Q2. When was Harekrushna Mahatab born? + 
 Ans . Harekrushna Mahatab was born on 21 November 1899 in Agarpada village, Bhadrak district, Odisha.
 Q3. Why is Harekrushna Mahatab known as Utkal Keshari? + 
 Ans . He is popularly known as Utkal Keshari, meaning Lion of Odisha, for his contributions to the freedom movement and Odisha's development.
 Q4. How many times did Harekrushna Mahatab serve as Chief Minister of Odisha? + 
 Ans . He served as Chief Minister of Odisha twice, from 1946 to 1950 and from 1956 to 1960.
 Q5. What were the major contributions of Harekrushna Mahatab? + 
 Ans . His major contributions include Odisha's princely state integration, shifting the capital to Bhubaneswar, the Hirakud Dam Project and promotion of literature and social reform.
